what: The registry's C_16 enclosure (maximusrufus, teorth/optimizationproblems #246, merged 2026-10-26 with both rows asterisked) decided as a second party by two implementations that share no code with each other or with the claimant's checkers (kept as text, never run): every finite claim of the two certificates, stated in corpus/optconst-queue/c16-2026-10-27/claims.json before deciding; the analytic steps (the weighted Cauchy–Schwarz dual bound, the tail bounds, the asymptotic bound g) read and re-derived there, never given a verdict; the convexity step not used (each box decided by subdivision with monotone enclosures)

pr.title: C_16: certified upper bound 2.1562256466 (enclosure with the #226 lower bound)
pr.author: maximusrufus

wordWhy: lower: every finite claim CERTIFIED by both implementations; the one reading (LR1: Parseval on [0, 2π]², the normalisation) is the definition applied to one explicit u, as in optq-226-16a. upper: the finite core CERTIFIED by both (UF1–UF3: the tiling, all 84 boxes against the printed digits, g(D0); and UF4's U_rational <= the printed digits); the step from it to C_16 <= 2.1562256466 crosses three analytic steps that are READ (UR1 the weighted Cauchy–Schwarz bound, UR2 the tail bounds with Σ|k|⁻⁴ = (2π²/3)G, UR4 F <= g for δ >= e and its supremum on [D0, ∞)), re-derived in claims.json — hence PARTIAL under the house grammar

LF2.note: the brackets contain the exact sums and the rational is below the exact value (Python, exact at 2^-200); the JavaScript decider, at double precision, sees the brackets meet its enclosures and cannot separate the rational, which sits ~1.3e-15 below the exact value (REFUSED at its precision)

boxBounds.note: a printed box bound is the claimant's float at R = 2000; the Python decider's looser tail (R = 1000) cannot reach the small-μ boxes and the JavaScript decider's doubles cannot separate the two g-boxes, whose printed bound is g(d1) to the last ulp; no box bound is below its formula in either; UF4 bears on nothing in the enclosure (UF2 decides the boxes against the printed digits directly)

UR1.statement: for every μ > 0 and δ >= 1: F(δ) <= B_μ(δ) := S1(μ)(1 + μδ)/π − ln δ − ln(1 + ln δ), S1(μ) = Σ_{k≠0} 1/(|k|²(1 + μ|k|²))
UR1.reason: an inequality between infinite sums; three lines, re-derived here

UR2.statement: for R >= 2 and T = R − √2: Σ_{|k|>R} 1/(|k|²(1 + μ|k|²)) <= min( (Z2 − P2(R))/μ , π ln(1 + 1/(μT²)) + π√2/T ), where P2(R) = Σ_{0<|k|<=R} |k|⁻⁴ and Z2 = Σ_{k≠0} |k|⁻⁴ = 4ζ(2)β(2) = (2π²/3)G, G Catalan's constant
UR2.reason: bounds on an infinite sum; (A) rests on a classical identity, (B) on an integral comparison; both re-derived here. The value of G and π are computed, not read.

UR3.statement: B_μ is convex in δ on [1, ∞), so its maximum over a box is attained at an endpoint (the claimant's step between boxes)
UR3.reason: correct, and NOT USED: the replay decides every box by subdivision with monotone enclosures (FINITE UF2), so no verdict rests on convexity
UR3.used: not used: every box is decided by subdivision

UR4.statement: with R0 = 100, T0 = R0 − √2, H = Σ_{0<|k|<=R0} |k|⁻², K = H/π + √2/T0 − 2 ln T0: for every δ >= e, F(δ) <= g(δ) := 1 + K + (K + ln ln δ)/ln δ + 2T0²/(δ ln δ); and sup_{δ >= D0} g(δ) <= g(D0) when ln D0 >= 1 and K + ln ln D0 >= 1
UR4.reason: the claimant's g is stated in the checker with its derivation in certify_c16_upper.py, which is NOT in the repository; re-derived here from the write-up's 'μ = 1/(δ ln δ)' and found to be the same function

UR5.statement: a LOWER bound for the same tail, used only for lower ends of enclosures (refutations, red controls), never for a certification: with T' = R + √2, Σ_{|k|>R} 1/(|k|²(1 + μ|k|²)) >= max(0, π ln(1 + 1/(μT'²)) − π√2 · min(1/T', 1/(3μT'³)))

LR1.statement: For the real zero-mean trigonometric polynomial u = Σ_{0 < |k|² ≤ R²} c_k e^{ik·x}, c_k = 1/(|k|²(1 + μ|k|²)) (c_k = c_{−k}), Parseval on [0, 2π]² gives u(0) = S1, ‖∇u‖² = 4π² S2, ‖Δu‖² = 4π² S3, with (the certificate's names, n = |k|², r₂(n) lattice points of norm n, c_n = q/(n(q + pn)), μ = p/q) S1 = Σ r₂(n) c_n, S2 = Σ r₂(n) n c_n², S3 = Σ r₂(n) n² c_n². Normalising ũ = u/‖∇u‖: Θ(δ_u) ≥ S1²/(4π² S2) at δ_u = S3/S2, so L ≥ F(δ_u) ≥ S1²/(π S2) − ln δ_u − ln(1 + ln δ_u), provided δ_u >= 1.
LR1.reason: definitional: the sup in Θ and the max in L applied to one explicit u; Parseval on the 2π-torus. The same reading as optq-226-16a (2026-10-16).

findings: the enclosure holds as printed: 2.1562247706 <= C_16 <= 2.1562256466 (upper: PARTIAL as above)

the boxes support 2.1562256458 (the largest endpoint value, box 31, μ = 0.12206997134993264, is 2.1562256407495 … 2.1562256457523); the printed 2.1562256466 and the certificate's U = 2.1562256465510830 are conservative by ~8e-10 (each printed box bound sits ~5–8e-10 above its endpoint maximum: the certifier's float64 error factor)
the trial polynomial's exact value is 2.15622477064423579034 … 2.15622477064423579035 (Python; JavaScript 2.1562247706441 … 2.1562247706444); the printed 2.1562247706 is its floor at ten places

the certificate's float fields slip by 1e-12 against their own rationals: L_lower_bound_float_rounded_down = 2.1562247706432345 while float(L_lower_bound_rational) = 2.1562247706442346 (harmless: lower), and U = 2.1562256465520826 while float(U_rational) = 2.1562256465510825 (harmless: higher)

neither checker's VERIFIED is the printed inequality: the lower checker accepts |L_lo − claimed| < 1e-9, the upper accepts U_v <= U + 1e-9 (at R = 1000); both inequalities are decided here against the printed digits directly

the certifiers named in the checkers (certify_c16_upper.py, certify_c16_lower.py) are not in the repository; the asymptotic g they use is re-derived in claims.json UR4 and agrees with the checker's formula
the registry's numerical row ≈ 2.15627 [BDZ2013] lies above the upper end: any value printing as 2.15627 is >= 2.156265 > 2.1562256466

printedMinusOneUnit.how: implied: 2.1562256458 <= 2.1562256465 and 2.1562256458 is CERTIFIED (the acceptance test is monotone in the bound)

redControls.what: C_16 <= 2.1562256457, one unit in the tenth place below the bound the boxes support (2.1562256458): box 31 (its endpoint value 2.1562256407495 … 2.1562256457523) cannot be closed
C_16 >= 2.1562247707 from the same trial polynomial (the printed lower bound one unit up): its value 2.1562247706441… is below
box 31 (μ = 0.12206997134993264) with its printed bound 2.1562256465510825 replaced by 2.1562256407485436, below the lower end of its endpoint maximum 2.1562256407495
box 40 removed from the tiling of [1, D0]

a mutant decider with S1(μ) taken as its partial sum over |k| <= 2000 alone (the UR2 tail omitted) certifies C_16 <= 2.1562240, below the certified lower end 2.1562247706 — caught by the crossing; the full decider cannot close box 31 on the same claim (REFUSED)

limits: the upper end's step from the finite core to the constant is analytic (UR1, UR2, UR4) and read, not computed
the lower end is a value of F at one explicit u; it says nothing about where the maximum is

the two deciders share the mathematics (the monotone enclosures of B_μ and g; the dual bound) and no code; they differ in the partial-sum radius (2000 here, 1000 in Python), in G (an alternating bracket here, Ramanujan's series there), in the r₂ table (divisor sieve here, octant enumeration there) and in the box method (monotone subdivision here, derivative-sign tests there)
